nightly-ci-bot: [ALERT] Nightly perf suite failed: p50 token latency +18% vs baseline on nightly/large-seq (seq=2048, model=gptj-6b-quant). CI job: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/12345 :eyes:
maria: ugh. notable regression window is 02:00-02:30 UTC. anyone on infra changes?
akshay: I merged batching micro-optim last night (PR #432). also upgraded redis staging from 6.2.10 -> 6.2.11 earlier today; shouldn't affect production but worth checking.
jen: tagging @akshay @sam to look at redis metrics.
sam: I already pulled metrics — there's a small spike in redis p95 (~30ms) around 02:05. I'll post the graf link in a sec <https://grafana/redwood/d/xyz>?view=redis
ioana: could be eviction pressure if key cardinality changed. any feature that changed prefixing?
akshay: we switched KV-prefixing to include session-id to reduce cross-session collisions. That increases key churn.
maria: that would increase cold misses + network roundtrips. can we isolate by running bench with a local in-process KV?
jen: yes — try OVERRIDE_KV=local for the bench: 
```
./bench/run.sh --suite nightly --model gptj-6b --seq 2048 --env OVERRIDE_KV=local
```
akshay: kicking that off on an m60 node now, posting results when done.
sam: also let's bisect between commits a1b2c3 (yesterday) and d4e5f6 (two days ago) if needed. akshay can you run bisect?
akshay: starting bisect, will keep updates here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: if bisect points at batching change we can revert quickly; if it's redis we need a pin/eviction tweak.
nightly-ci-bot: queued job 12347: bench run with OVERRIDE_KV=local (owner: akshay)
akshay: first OVERRIDE_KV=local run finished — p50 is back to baseline (~+1%). local run logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/12347/logs
jen: that strongly suggests KV network dependency. can you run with an in-memory redis instance to be certain?
akshay: on it, spinning up ephemeral redis on same host.
kevin: infra note — we rotated a couple redis nodes at 01:40 UTC due to memory pressure from a customer job. rotation may have triggered evictions. I'll inspect eviction_count and aof/rdb events.
sam: thanks, kevin. if rotations correlate we'll need an ops mitigation: pin versions or adjust autoscaling.
ioana: action items so far: akshay run in-memory redis test + complete bisect if any reg remains; kevin verify rotation/eviction metrics; maria sketch rollback/mitigation plan (pin or eviction policy change).
akshay: in-memory redis run confirmed: p50 stable, matches OVERRIDE_KV=local. looks like redis evictions/churn are the cause. bisect didn't show a code regression — bisect pointed to infra time window.
maria: ok, I'll prepare a canary mitigation: set maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru -> volatile-lru? or temporarily increase redis memory and pin version if rotation was buggy. prepping PR and runbook.
jen: ping me on the PR for quick review, I can approve and help rollout.
kevin: found eviction spikes and RDB saves during rotation window. rolling back that rotation and bumping memory for the cluster would reduce evictions. I'll schedule a controlled rotation with zero-eviction policy tomorrow 03:00 UTC if we want.
sam: can we add a short-term software fallback too? eg. enable local KV-client-side cache to reduce trips for hot prefixes.
akshay: I can enable client-side LRU cache in the runtime as a quick patch and test impact. will open PR.
maria: thanks everyone — agreed plan: (1) akshay patch client-side cache + test, (2) kevin revert/redo rotation with safer config, (3) maria prepare rollback runbook and canary, (4) jen review PRs. follow-up in #eng-runtime tomorrow AM if anything flaps. :thumbsup:
jen: sounds good. if anything else crops up, @here.
nightly-ci-bot: monitoring resumed, will post if nightly fails again.
